question: Which three cities have the largest difference between their 1990 EPA PM2.5 measurements (using units_of_measure = 'Micrograms/cubic meter (LC)' and parameter_name = 'Acceptable PM2.5 AQI & Speciation Mass') and their 2020 OpenAQ PM2.5 measurements (where pollutant = 'pm25' based on the year extracted from the timestamp), with both datasets matched by latitude and longitude rounded to two decimals, and the difference ordered from greatest to least?
sql:
SELECT 
  o.city as city_name,
  ROUND(e.lat, 2) as lat,
  ROUND(e.lon, 2) as lon,
  e.avg_epa_pm25,
  o.avg_openaq_pm25,
  e.avg_epa_pm25 - o.avg_openaq_pm25 as difference
FROM (
  SELECT ROUND(latitude, 2) as lat, ROUND(longitude, 2) as lon, AVG(arithmetic_mean) as avg_epa_pm25
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.air_quality_annual_summary`
  WHERE year = 1990
    AND units_of_measure = 'Micrograms/cubic meter (LC)'
    AND parameter_name = 'Acceptable PM2.5 AQI & Speciation Mass'
    AND arithmetic_mean IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY lat, lon
) e
JOIN (
  SELECT city, ROUND(latitude, 2) as lat, ROUND(longitude, 2) as lon, AVG(value) as avg_openaq_pm25
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.openaq.global_air_quality`
  WHERE pollutant = 'pm25'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) = 2020
    AND value IS NOT NULL
    AND city IS NOT NULL
    AND city != ''
    AND city != 'N/A'
  GROUP BY city, lat, lon
) o
ON e.lat = o.lat AND e.lon = o.lon
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 3
